skill.description: Guides end users through Snowflake access requests, RSA key setup, Snow CLI and Python connection examples, and first-session troubleshooting for SnowTower.
skill.summary: Guides SnowTower users through Snowflake access, key setup, connection, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: Database-Tycoon

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, SQL examples, public-key references, and access request form text. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found, but the skill does recommend an unencrypted Snowflake private key, which is a real credential risk.

remediation.suggestion: Recommend encrypted private keys or an approved secret store, and remove -nocrypt and private_key_file_pwd=None from examples.

remediation.issue: Credential handling instructions need stronger guardrails
remediation.suggestion: State that private keys must never be pasted into chats, tickets, logs, or AI prompts, and include key rotation guidance.

remediation.issue: Local command examples may be run by tool-enabled agents
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit instruction that key-generation commands require user confirmation and should run only on the user-owned workstation.

content.value_statement: New data users often need help requesting Snowflake access and connecting correctly. This skill gives a guided SnowTower workflow for access requests, RSA keys, Snow CLI, Python, and common errors.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through Snowflake access request steps for SnowTower.
Explains how to prepare RSA key material for Snowflake authentication.
Shows Snow CLI connection setup and basic connection testing.
Provides a Python connector example using key pair authentication.
Explains default roles, warehouses, and personal database expectations.
Troubleshoots authentication, privilege, warehouse, and connection issues.
limitations: It does not approve access or modify Snowflake accounts.
It cannot verify organization-specific account names, roles, or warehouses.
Command examples must be reviewed before users run them locally.
It does not replace administrator security policies or key management rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First Access Request
use_cases.description: Create a clear checklist for generating a public key and submitting a SnowTower access issue.

use_cases.title: Connect a Local Workflow
use_cases.description: Understand the connection details needed for Snow CLI or a Python data workflow.

use_cases.title: Resolve Common Access Errors
use_cases.description: Map common Snowflake login, role, warehouse, and key problems to practical next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start My Access Request
prompt_templates.prompt: I am a new SnowTower user. Walk me through what I need before I submit a Snowflake access request.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Connection Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Snowflake connection details and tell me what information I still need from the administrator.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: I cannot connect to Snowflake with key pair authentication. Ask targeted questions and give a safe troubleshooting sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Onboarding
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SnowTower onboarding checklist for a team that needs Snowflake roles, warehouses, and personal databases.

output_examples.input: I need Snowflake access for analytics work. What should I do first?
output: Generate a Snowflake public key on your local machine.
Keep the private key private and submit only the public key.
Open the access request form and include your name, team, reason, and public key.
Wait for approval before configuring Snow CLI or Python.

output_examples.input: My Snowflake key authentication fails after approval.
output: Confirm that your account name, user name, and role match the approval message.
Check that the private key path points to the file you generated.
Verify that file permissions are restrictive.
Compare the submitted public key with the public key derived from your private key.

output_examples.input: What do I get after SnowTower approval?
output: You usually receive a user name, account identifier, default role, and default warehouse.
You may also receive a personal development database for safe analysis work.
Use your assigned role and warehouse when testing your first query.

best_practices: Submit only the public key in access requests.
Confirm account identifiers and roles from the approval message before connecting.
Use the smallest practical warehouse and stop expensive queries quickly.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private keys into chat, tickets, or access requests.
Do not run setup commands without checking what files they create or modify.
Do not request broad production access without a specific business reason.

faq.question: Can this skill approve my Snowflake access?
faq.answer: No. It explains the request process, but an administrator must approve access.

faq.question: What key should I submit in the access request?
faq.answer: Submit only the public key. Never submit the private key.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it create my Snowflake connection automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users must review before running.

faq.question: What problems can it troubleshoot?
faq.answer: It covers authentication failures, insufficient privileges, suspended warehouses, and incorrect connection details.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for security policy?
faq.answer: No. Follow your organization policy for keys, passwords, MFA, rotation, and account access.
